scenes.line1: How do apps handle secure login?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how apps keep your login secure and tokens out of the wrong hands? Let’s break down OAuth and OpenID Connect flows.

scenes.label: OAuth 2.0
scenes.sub: Lets apps ask for access without sharing your password.
scenes.say: OAuth two lets apps request access to your data without ever seeing your password.

scenes.label: OIDC
scenes.sub: OpenID Connect adds authentication on top of OAuth.
scenes.say: OpenID Connect builds on OAuth, adding authentication so apps know who you are.

rows.b: Server sends code to the app
App swaps code plus PKCE for tokens

scenes.say: Here’s the secure flow: The app sends you to log in, gets a code back, then trades that code and a secret PKCE value for tokens. This blocks attackers from stealing your tokens.

scenes.question: What does PKCE prevent?
scenes.right: It stops attackers from intercepting the code and using it to get tokens.
scenes.say: Here’s a classic interview trap: PKCE isn’t about encrypting tokens—it’s about stopping code interception attacks.
